sql: SELECT label_id FROM labels INNER JOIN boards_epic_lists ON boards_epic_lists.label_id = labels.id INNER JOIN boards_epic_boards ON boards_epic_boards.id = boards_epic_lists.epic_board_id WHERE boards_epic_lists.list_type = 1 AND boards_epic_boards.id = 1
notes: Label has_many :epic_lists (EE). boards_epic_lists is the joined side: label_id = labels.id, and epic_board_id = boards_epic_boards.id = const, so the whole key (epic_board_id, label_id) is determined; movable (list_type IN [label]) gives list_type = 1, which is the predicate. Each label matches at most one epic list, so the join does not duplicate labels, and the boards_epic_boards join could be dropped (epic_board_id = const). Used by Label.ids_on_epic_board <- ee/app/services/boards/epics/move_service.rb:28. pluck(:label_id) emits an unqualified label_id that resolves to boards_epic_lists.label_id; the Label default_scope ORDER BY labels.title is also appended. Also EpicList validates :label_id uniqueness scope epic_board_id if label? (no list_type in the SQL).

The model (Gitlab::Database::BackgroundOperation::WorkerCellLocal) lives in lib/, outside the checkout. The only in-scope query filters by gitlab_schema/job_class_name, not the index key + status IN (0,1,2).

sql: SELECT cd_applications.* FROM cd_applications WHERE cd_applications.id IN (SELECT cd_rollouts.application_id FROM cd_rollouts WHERE cd_rollouts.state = 1 AND cd_rollouts.organization_id = 1)
notes: cd_rollouts is the inner (subquery) side; the semi-join compares application_id (the whole key, and IN implies NOT NULL), and in_progress (state = 1) implies state IN (0,1,2). Subquery rows are unique on application_id, so the IN semi-join can become a plain join with no dedup. Used by with_status('deploying').
